text:
Leaky gut (Phase 5): a widespread inflammatory condition often intersecting with other categories of illness such as Crohn's Disease or irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), plant food intolerance, and what many alternative health practitioners consider as a root cause of most diseases. It's associated clinically with increased levels of zonulin, the molecule released to open your intestinal tight junctions, the seals between the cells of your gut lining. Too much opening time leads to allowing stuff to leak out into your blood stream which then burdens your immune system and detoxification systems. Game-changing treatments:

Liposomal first-milking colostrum, the first milk a cow makes after giving birth, wrapped in tiny fat bubbles that help you absorb it (esp. fermented per Matt Nedin's protocol with bifidobacterium, a common probiotic, or SIBO yogurt bacteria). Matt from EndSickness.org finds that this helps especially to mop up mycotoxins, the toxins molds make, in the gut. Activated charcoal can also be helpful, altho don't take that with things you want to actually absorb.
section: Some Causes of poor gut health
reader: Someone with poor gut health reading the plant-food and leaky gut causes, choosing among the leaky gut treatments the list gives, who has never heard of zonulin, colostrum or BPC-157.

sentences.s: Leaky gut (Phase 5): a widespread inflammatory condition often intersecting with other categories of illness such as Crohn's Disease or irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), plant food intolerance, and what many alternative health practitioners consider as a root cause of most diseases.
sentences.payoff: IBS gets its full name at its first mention, so its own item later and the stacks section read without guessing.
sentences.follows: It opens the leaky gut cause after the plant-food one it overlaps with, as before.

sentences.s: It's associated clinically with increased levels of zonulin, the molecule released to open your intestinal tight junctions, the seals between the cells of your gut lining.
sentences.payoff: The reader learns what zonulin does (it opens the tight junctions) and what tight junctions are (the seals between the gut lining's cells) in the sentence that first names them, so the leaking in the next sentence and the fuels later make sense.
sentences.follows: It says how leaky gut shows up, right after what leaky gut is, as his two sentences did; joined, so zonulin is explained where it is named.

sentences.s: Too much opening time leads to allowing stuff to leak out into your blood stream which then burdens your immune system and detoxification systems.

Liposomal first-milking colostrum, the first milk a cow makes after giving birth, wrapped in tiny fat bubbles that help you absorb it (esp. fermented per Matt Nedin's protocol with bifidobacterium, a common probiotic, or SIBO yogurt bacteria).
sentences.payoff: The reader knows what they'd be buying (a cow's first milk, in fat bubbles that help it absorb) at the item's name, before how Matt's protocol ferments it.
sentences.follows: It opens the list of leaky gut treatments the item above announced.

sentences.s: Matt from EndSickness.org finds that this helps especially to mop up mycotoxins, the toxins molds make, in the gut.
sentences.payoff: The reader learns mycotoxins are mold toxins at their first mention, so the colostrum's job and the mold check in Phase 6 make sense.
sentences.follows: It gives what the colostrum is good for after saying what it is.

sentences.s: Activated charcoal can also be helpful, altho don't take that with things you want to actually absorb.

checked.point: zonulin opens the tight junctions between the gut lining's cells
checked.found: Sturgeon and Fasano 2016: zonulin is the only known physiological modulator of the tight junctions between cells, and more of it means a leakier barrier (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/28123927)
checked.still_needed: yes: the leaking in the next sentence depends on it

checked.point: colostrum is the first milk after giving birth; liposomal means in fat bubbles that help absorption
checked.found: bovine colostrum is the first milk a cow's mammary gland makes after calving (https://www.alice.cnptia.embrapa.br/alice/bitstream/doc/1135735/1/Bovine-colostrum.pdf); liposomal supplements put the nutrient inside tiny spheres of phospholipid, a fat, which can protect it in digestion and often help absorption (https://neuroganhealth.com/blogs/news/liposomal-vs-capsule-supplements)

checked.point: BPC-157 is lab-made, based on a stomach juice protein
checked.found: a synthetic 15-amino-acid peptide derived from a protein in human gastric juice (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BPC-157)
checked.still_needed: yes: it shows why the plant claim is false

checked.point: resistant starch is starch the body can't digest, so it reaches the gut bacteria
checked.found: starch that escapes digestion in the small intestine and is fermented by the bacteria in the colon (https://www.frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/fnut.2024.1369950/full)
checked.still_needed: yes: it is why it feeds them

checked.point: zeolite is a volcanic mineral full of pores
checked.found: porous minerals, mostly from volcanic ash (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30999685/)
checked.still_needed: yes: the pores are the point

placement: The plant-food cause and the leaky gut list, in his order; each explanation inside the sentence that first names the term, the colostrum and BPC-157 ones joined into their items instead of the sentences after them.

questions.Q1: PASS: each term is explained in the sentence that first uses it (zonulin, tight junctions, colostrum, liposomal, BPC-157, resistant starch, FODMAP), none in a sentence after; each sentence's point comes before its explanation (resistant starch's job, then why; Phase 2's aim, then whose it is)
questions.Q2: PASS: the only instructions are his (go Paleo-Low FODMAP or Low Fermentation Eating; no snacking) and Phase 2's opening, which says what the reader does (calm the inflammation down and starve the overgrowths)
questions.Q3: PASS: each explanation names the exact thing (the seals between the cells of your gut lining; the first milk a cow makes after giving birth; the carbs they ferment most easily)
questions.Q4: PASS: zonulin, tight junctions, colostrum, liposomal, BPC-157, beta-glucans, resistant starch and FODMAPs are explained once, where first used; mycotoxins and bifidobacterium were explained in try 1; vitamins and common words left alone
questions.Q5: PASS: the "since" in the resistant starch and FODMAP sentences each give the reason for the point before them; "Once the mechanics work" turns on Phase 1's point
questions.Q6: PASS: nothing moved between paragraphs; inside them, Phase 2 now says what it does before whose it is
questions.Q7: PASS: each explanation is what a reader needs to buy or follow the item it is in
questions.Q8: PASS: no item moved between groups
questions.Q9: PASS: "no harsh chemicals" uncompressed to "without any harsh chemicals"; each explanation is a clause of the sentence that uses the term, one step each

question_text.Q1: Why am I reading this sentence, and do I know it before I have to work through it? (the point first, in each sentence and each paragraph; a study after the question it answers; a term explained where it is first used, never in a sentence after it)
question_text.Q2: What is each instruction for, said in the reader's terms, and is it something the helper does ("have someone go with them"), not a rule stated as a fact ("someone goes with them")?
question_text.Q3: Which thing exactly? (pools of water, not water; any substance, not anything)
question_text.Q4: What does each word act on, or mean here? (adjunct remedy; known-genuine) Is every term a high-school graduate wouldn't know (enterocytes, BPC-157) explained once, where it is first used, and common ones (a vitamin) left alone?
question_text.Q5: Why does each sentence follow from the one before? (every but, so, because and this has what it turns on)
question_text.Q6: Is this the order the reader is thinking in, and does each idea sit next to what it continues?
question_text.Q7: Does each fact help this reader now, in their case (the same kind of thing they face, not just the same topic)?
question_text.Q8: Does each item belong in the group it is put in?
question_text.Q9: Is anything compressed? (one step a sentence, the small words that carry the relation, no space before mg)
